cells.tense: You stand inside the tangled thing right now, holding the pen.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Call to mind something you owe one person — a thank-you, a return, a repair — and settle it before anyone asks.
cells.core:
You can take a mess between two people and set the pieces out until they line up. That isn't coldness. It's what lets you walk into a room where both sides are half-right and still say the sentence that holds, and the people in there feel the difference. Where you feel with someone rather than just about them, it works because you aren't deciding who wins.

The part that's yours is smaller than it looks. Something you owe one person and haven't gotten to — a thank-you, a thing given back, a small repair — settle it without waiting to be reminded. Not because a tally says so. Because the sense of fairness already tells you which one it is, and doing that one is what makes the rest of the gathering easy.

cells.tense: You will have the whole conversation mapped before the other person sits down.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Take the thing you keep pushing toward and do its next piece at a speed you could hold for a month.
cells.core:
Where you feel with someone rather than just about them, the gathering runs fast now, in front of the moment. The shape of the talk is worked out before they sit down, and each rehearsal makes the real one feel less safe, so you rehearse again. The feeling underneath gets skipped in the service of being ready. What people meet is the plan.

And the plan has nothing to land on. This tempo outruns the thing itself, and what you're braced for rarely arrives the way you wrote it. So take the thing you keep pushing toward and do its next piece at a speed you could hold for a month, not the pace you could hold for a day. Your own sense of timing will tell you when it's real; you don't have to know in advance.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door the room has already moved past.
cells.act: rest in the connection without doing anything with it
cells.ask: Give an hour to someone or something you love and do nothing with it — no fixing, no talking it through, no task.
cells.core:
Where you feel with someone rather than just about them, you are a step back from the moment now. The gathering still happens — you can line up each side of it — but you do it from the far side of the door, and when you come in, part of you stays out. The feeling is thin, not gone. You haven't been adding to it, so it has less to hold. Nothing is broken. The account just needs a deposit.

Rest in a connection without doing anything with it. An hour with someone you love, or with something you love, no fixing, no talking it through, no task. No outcome to check for. What you feel in that hour is the material the next real conversation gets made of, and it returns without being summoned.

cells.tense: You are holding a group together and calling it nothing much.
cells.act: celebrate with the others, not after them
cells.ask: When something good lands for someone near you, mark it with them — go to them, not the retelling.
cells.core:
You can gather the loose threads of a group — the thing that needs saying, the person who needs hearing — and you do it so smoothly it disappears into the background. The skill is real. You have filed it under being easy to be around, or under someone else needing more than you do. Nobody hands it back, because nobody sees it happen, and from where you stand you don't see it either.

So let the gladness go out to the room while it's warm. When something good lands for someone near you, mark it with them instead of hearing about it later. It isn't pay for anything. It's the plainest version of the connection you already build, done in the open, and that is where you get to watch it belong to you.
cells.sheetLine: Holding the group together reads to you as nothing much.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person has been quietly misattributing a genuine relational gift to circumstances or to other people's doing; the record names no such history, so Unacknowledged is written only as the capacity operating out of view, with the person free to say no. A reader could reasonably object that gathering thoughts into a strategy before speaking is just how anyone handles a hard conversation, and that calling it a gift over-reads ordinary tact. The asks survive being wrong: each one is a small act of the person's own medicine, checkable by whether the fair thing got done or the feeling got its pace, not by whether my read of them is right. The sentence that serves my draft more than the person is the one that makes them sound like the steady one everybody leans on — cut it, they never claimed that role here.
